clue.text: They manage change half-heartedly

indicators.note: the doubled letter at the heart of the word loses one of its pair, half its centre

parts.note: coppers are low-value coins, small change in British slang

explanation.surface: Someone who manages to alter things only with half a heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-heartedly' drops one of the two central Ps of COPPERS. 'manage' here means cope, not run a business.
explanation.definitionFit: People who cope with difficulty are copers: they manage, getting by somehow.

clue.text: Clowns often making idiotic comments say, originally

definitions.text: Clowns often making idiotic comments say, originally

indicators.note: originally means taking the starting letter of each of the preceding six words

explanation.surface: Clowns tend to come out with foolish remarks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both definition and wordplay: the first letters of the six words before 'originally' spell the answer, and those clowns are what the clue describes.
explanation.definitionFit: Comedians are often called comics, clowns who make idiotic comments for laughs.

clue.text: Solid forward covering player with Everton's wingers

indicators.note: covering means the word for forward wraps around the following pieces

parts.note: pert means forward or cheeky
a man is a player in a team or a board game

indicators.note: the wingers of a word are its two outside letters, here those of the football club's name

explanation.surface: A sturdy striker marks a footballer, flanked by Everton's wide men.
explanation.walkthrough: Everton is a Liverpool football club; its wingers are its first and last letters. 'covering' wraps the forward word around the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Something solid and lasting is permanent: fixed rather than temporary.

clue.text: Republican centre supporter brought up nonsense

parts.note: a hub is a centre of activity

indicators.note: in a down clue, brought up means the word for supporter is written upwards, reversed

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment

explanation.surface: A Republican at the heart of things talks rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' reverses BRA to ARB at the foot of the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhubarb is British slang for nonsense or meaningless chatter, from the word actors mutter as crowd noise.

clue.text: Considered well upset seeing drunk outside

indicators.note: outside means the drink word goes around the other piece

parts.note: supped is a past tense of sup, to drink

indicators.note: upset means the little word for well is turned over, reversed

parts.note: so, as in 'so, what now?', is a filler like well

explanation.surface: Thought to be quite upset after seeing someone drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like an anagram signal but is a past tense of sup; 'seeing' only links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something considered or assumed to be so is supposed: believed, taken as given.

clue.text: Employs American round outskirts of Seattle

indicators.note: round means the American letters wrap around the other piece
outskirts of a word are its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A firm hires an American around the edge of Seattle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' wraps the American letters around the city's outer pair.
explanation.definitionFit: To employ a tool or method is to make use of it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Swears, parking, left on rims

parts.note: P stands for parking on road signs
rims are the edges of things

explanation.surface: A driver curses on parking with the tyres against the kerb.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests cursing; the definition means making solemn promises.
explanation.definitionFit: Swears in the sense of vows: one who swears to do something makes solemn promises.

clue.text: Faint shortly overcoming wife

indicators.note: overcoming is read as going over and around, so the word for shortly contains the letter for wife

parts.note: shortly means soon, before long

explanation.surface: Someone about to faint any minute, overpowering his wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' looks like a cut-short signal but just means SOON.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to lose consciousness briefly, as in a fainting fit.

clue.text: Horror of nudist as teacher

indicators.note: of signals that the answer is taken from within the following words, part of them

explanation.surface: The shock of discovering one's teacher is a naturist.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'nuDIST AS TEacher'.
explanation.definitionFit: Distaste is strong dislike or aversion, a milder form of horror.

clue.text: Double short knocked back creates complaint

indicators.note: knocked back, as a drink is downed, means the doubled letters are read backwards
Double means the drink word is written twice in a row

parts.note: a short is a small measure of spirits, such as rum

explanation.surface: Downing a double measure of spirits leads to grumbling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Double' gives RUMRUM and 'knocked back' turns it round. 'short' looks like a cut but is a spirit.
explanation.definitionFit: A murmur is a low grumble, a complaint voiced quietly.

clue.text: Liberal low-down love god embraces you say

parts.note: gen is British slang for information, the low-down

indicators.note: embraces means the god's name holds the other piece inside

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

indicators.note: say means the word you is spoken, giving the letter that sounds like it

parts.note: the word you

explanation.surface: A broad-minded tip-off: the love god hugs you, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns 'you' into U; 'embraces' puts it inside EROS. 'Liberal' here means open-handed, not the political party.
explanation.definitionFit: A liberal helping is a generous one: free-handed, plentiful.

clue.text: Overpower some trespasser perhaps, getting upended

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting upended means the hidden letters are read from the bottom up
some means only part of the following words is taken

explanation.surface: Subduing an intruder, perhaps by tipping him over.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards within 'trespaSSER PERhaps'.
explanation.definitionFit: To repress is to put down or subdue by force, to overpower.

clue.text: Parlour game had races, unfortunately

indicators.note: unfortunately suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters come out in a muddled order

explanation.surface: The family game turned into races, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Charades is a classic indoor party game of miming words for others to guess.

clue.text: Elderly beginning to adore absorbing new programme

indicators.note: absorbing means the earlier letters take in the letter for new

parts.note: aged means elderly

indicators.note: beginning to means taking the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: An old person starts loving a new TV show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'absorbing' places N inside AGEDA, the letters for elderly plus the first of 'adore'.
explanation.definitionFit: An agenda is a list or programme of items to be dealt with.

clue.text: Democrat winds up giving threats

parts.note: to wind someone up is to annoy them, so it angers them

explanation.surface: A Democratic politician provokes people by issuing threats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'winds up' means annoys here, not finishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Dangers are hazards or menaces, things that threaten harm.

clue.text: Humiliation as member rants drunkenly

indicators.note: drunkenly suggests unsteady staggering, so the letters reel into a new order

explanation.surface: The shame of an MP ranting while drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Embarrassment is the feeling of shame or loss of dignity that humiliation brings.

clue.text: Face of First Lady almost wreathed in joy

indicators.note: wreathed in means the shortened name is surrounded by the joy word

parts.note: elation is great joy

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the name is dropped

parts.note: Eve is the first woman in the Bible

explanation.surface: The First Lady's face nearly wreathed in happiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First Lady' looks like a president's wife but is Eve, the first woman; 'Face' means a side of a building.
explanation.definitionFit: An elevation is an architectural drawing of one face or side of a building.

clue.text: Fuel resentment with being consumed by diet

indicators.note: being consumed by means the first pieces sit inside the word for diet, as if eaten

parts.note: diet is what one eats, food
ire is anger or resentment

explanation.surface: Stoking resentment by sticking to a diet.
explanation.walkthrough: W is a standard short form for 'with'; 'Fuel' looks like a verb but is a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Firewood is logs or sticks burnt as fuel.

clue.text: Obstinacy namely involves terribly stern caning

indicators.note: involves means the two letters for namely enclose the jumbled letters

parts.note: i.e. is the Latin abbreviation for that is, namely

indicators.note: terribly suggests something badly done, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Stubbornness, that is, takes in a severe beating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' rearranges STERN CANING into NTRANSIGENC, which 'involves' puts between I and E.
explanation.definitionFit: Intransigence is a refusal to compromise or change one's mind: stubbornness.

clue.text: Confident fool shamefaced about United

indicators.note: about means the first pieces go around the letter for United

parts.note: an ass is a fool
red-faced with shame, so red
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A cocky idiot blushing over a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts U inside ASSRED.
explanation.definitionFit: Assured means self-possessed and sure of oneself, confident.

clue.text: Pasta heaps with last of Parmesan topping

indicators.note: in a down clue, topping means this letter goes above the rest
last of means taking only the final letter of the cheese name

parts.note: oodles means heaps, a great amount

explanation.surface: Pasta piled high, finished off with a grating of Parmesan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topping' places N above OODLES in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Noodles are long strips of pasta.

clue.text: Dog set about heavy chow

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around into a new order

explanation.surface: A dog settles in to some hefty food, chow being both a breed and grub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chow' tempts as a dog breed, matching 'Dog'; here it means food.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, filling, starchy food: weighty grub.

clue.text: Catch he-men cavorting around top of stage

indicators.note: around means the jumbled letters go round the other one
cavorting means leaping about, so the letters are rearranged
top of means taking the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Musclemen prancing about on stage are caught.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cavorting' rearranges HEMEN into ENMEH; 'around' puts S inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To enmesh is to entangle as in a net, to catch.

clue.text: Melody imbues pitch occasionally

indicators.note: occasionally means only every other letter of the following words is used

explanation.surface: A tune that fills a football ground every so often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'occasionally' takes the even letters of 'imbues pitch'.
explanation.definitionFit: Music is organised sound, broadly a melody or tune.

clue.text: Feeling much better?

parts.note: reads like someone recovering from illness, but describes a person who feels far superior to others

explanation.surface: A kindly question to a recovering patient.
explanation.walkthrough: Recovery from illness is the false scent; the sense is feeling much better than everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: A haughty person thinks themself superior to others, feeling much better than them.

clue.text: Check return of Queen with popular support

indicators.note: in a down clue, support means this piece sits beneath the earlier one, holding it up
return of means the letters for the Queen are read backwards

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: Checking the Queen's comeback with public backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return of' turns ER into RE; 'support' puts IN beneath it.
explanation.definitionFit: To rein in is to check or restrain, as a rider does a horse.

clue.text: Old boy's always purchasing 'right' Spectator

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil, plus the S of the possessive

indicators.note: purchasing means taking on, so the word for always holds the letter for right

parts.note: ever means always

explanation.surface: An old school chum always buys the right-wing weekly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Spectator is a British magazine, a rival of The Observer newspaper, a deliberate red herring. 'purchasing' puts R inside EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectator is someone watching, an onlooker who observes.

clue.text: United scored wasting time

indicators.note: wasting means the letter for time is lost from the word

parts.note: to tally is to score or count up

explanation.surface: A football club scored while time-wasting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'United' looks like a team name but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Allied means joined together in alliance, united.

clue.text: Corrupt worthy accepts promotion

indicators.note: accepts means the word for worthy takes the promotion inside

parts.note: decent means worthy, respectable
an ad promotes a product

explanation.surface: A respectable person is bribed with a promotion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'promotion' suggests a job, but is advertising, so AD.
explanation.definitionFit: Decadent means morally decayed or self-indulgent, corrupt.

clue.text: Empty Anglican Church following American custom

indicators.note: following means the later pieces come after the letters for American
Empty means the inside letters are removed, leaving the two ends of the word

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A deserted Anglican church copying American practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty' leaves AN from Anglican.
explanation.definitionFit: Usance is an old word for usage or custom, now chiefly the time allowed for paying bills.
